message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held devices are illegal while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC). | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on the right. | | **School Bus** | • Stop for all vehicles when a school bus stops and displays red lights. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or fire hydrant.
• No parking on sidewalks unless marked. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for violations such as illegal parking, abandoned vehicles, or if they pose a hazard. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Vehicle inspections required for most vehicles (except exempt categories). | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras enforce speed limits; fines are issued automatically. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergency** | • Call 911 for emergencies.
• For non‑emergencies, use the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) roadside assistance hotline. | ### Where to Find Official Texts - **Texas Transportation Code** – The full statutory text is available online via the Texas Legislature’s website. - **TxDOT** – Provides guidelines, maps, and updates on road conditions. - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Offers driver’s handbook, registration forms, and inspection requirements. ### Common Enforcement Practices - **Speeding**: Police use radar guns; automated cameras also issue tickets. - **Seat‑belt & Child Seat**: Random checks; fines range from $50–$200 depending on violation. - **DUI**: Breathalyzer tests; penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. ### Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Plan for Long Distances** – Texas is large; plan fuel stops and rest breaks. 2. **Watch for Weather** – Sudden rain can cause slick roads; adjust speed accordingly. 3. **Use Navigation Aids** – GPS can help avoid congestion and find alternate routes. 4. **Stay Informed** – Follow TxDOT alerts for construction, detours, or closures. Feel free to let me know if you need deeper details on any specific law or how to handle a particular situation!
